static_traits.name: Lin Fan
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to chat about everyday topics with, but unwilling to discuss Self-doubt and negative thoughts with them; struggles to connect with hikers/outdoor enthusiasts due to Self-denial
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological distress; no history of psychotherapy; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to identify one's own thought patterns and trigger situations; neutral tone, good cooperativeness; tending toward self-criticism and negating positive feedback

basic_info.main_problem: I often negate the positive parts of my achievements; especially despite completing the Appalachian Trail, I still do not consider myself a good hiker. This leads to inferiority and Self-doubt.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes through methods such as reality testing to build a more realistic and more positive self-evaluation, based on past achievements rather than focusing on shortcomings, thereby restoring motivation and enjoyment in writing and outdoor activities.
growth_experiences: Last summer completed the long-distance hike of the Appalachian Trail, a highly difficult challenge. After this achievement, persistent Self-doubt and inferiority gradually emerged, especially noticeable when comparing with veteran hikers; when others give positive feedback on one's hiking or writing, often feeling they are just being polite or do not understand the real standards, thus quickly negating positive experiences.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / do not deserve recognition
Only meeting very high standards gives one value

special_situations.event: Comparing with senior hikers or thinking of their performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my performance does not reach the 'good hiker' standard and is not as good as theirs, it means I am no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces socializing with hikers, avoids outdoor activities to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am not a real hiker.

special_situations.event: Receives positive feedback from others about his hiking or writing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others praise me, it is mostly politeness or they do not understand the real standards
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, emphasizing inadequacy to maintain the 'I am not good enough' self-schema
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just saying nice things; I am actually not that good.

special_situations.event: When outdoor activities are mentioned or planned
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I go to outdoor activities, I will perform poorly and be seen through as not a good hiker
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Treats the outdoors as a burden and reduces participation to avoid 'exposure'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will mess up and be seen as not good enough.

special_situations.event: When recalling hiking experiences, attention turns to areas for improvement
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not done as well as others or perfectly, this achievement does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting excessively high standards, constantly nitpicking oneself to force progress
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: What I do is still not good enough, far from qualified.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and seen as competent (hopes one's efforts and achievements are truly seen)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being exposed as an 'incompetent' impostor, fearing judgment and rejection
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being negated by belittling achievements and Avoids socializing
Uses high standards and self-criticism to gain a sense of control, avoids feeling vulnerable

object_relations.self_representation: An 'impostor' who is not qualified and needs to constantly prove oneself
object_relations.object_representation: Harshly judging others who may expose one's inadequacy at any time (especially veteran hikers)

object_relations.self_representation: A striver whose achievements are ignored
object_relations.object_representation: Evaluators who are polite on the surface but not sincere (praise that does not 'count')

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others give positive feedback on one's hiking/writing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other person is just being polite or does not understand the real standards (Interpreting external positive information as ineffective)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in an understated tone, negating positive evaluations with words like 'they are just being polite''this is nothing', reducing emotional expression.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about comparison with senior hikers or discussing one's own achievements
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will negate me like my inner critic does, seeing through me (projecting self-criticism onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using vague and avoidant expressions, reducing details, and instead emphasizing one's own inadequacy; cautious tone, avoiding direct contact with others' affirmation.

manifestations: Finds it hard to connect with hikers/outdoor enthusiasts; worries about being seen as a fraud
Unwilling to discuss Self-doubt and negative thoughts with friends
outcomes: Increased Social avoidance and sense of isolation

manifestations: After completing a long-distance hike, finds it hard to gain lasting meaning from the achievement, positive emotions fade quickly
Focusing attention on inadequacy rather than value and meaning
outcomes: Decreased motivation (especially writing and outdoor activities)
Weakened sense of achievement and Self-efficacy

manifestations: Bound by the external standards and expectations of a 'good hiker', finding it hard to define achievement by one's own choices
Fearing judgment for not meeting standards, limiting self-expression and attempts
outcomes: Avoiding personally meaningful activities, reduced sense of Freedom in experiences

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly judging oneself by the external standard of 'good hiker', negating one's own achievements
Responding to others' affirmation with 'this does not count''not qualified'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Being highly critical of one's own performance, frequent Self-denial
Being overly cautious when communicating with fellow enthusiasts, worrying about exposing inadequacy

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Attributing inner self-criticism to others looking down on or exposing oneself
Interprets others' positive feedback as 'politeness' rather than genuine evaluation

exception_events.target_problem: When outdoor activities are mentioned or positive feedback from others is received, the client usually automatically negates the positive aspects, believing oneself not a good hiker, thereby reducing interest and motivation to participate.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At the moment of summiting certain difficult sections, he did not immediately belittle himself as usual, but felt proud, recognizing his own effort and persistence; this positive feeling lasted for a while.
exception_events.reason: Different situation: facing concrete and clear challenges with visible results; different approach: focusing on present experience and evidence of effort; different understanding: viewing overcoming difficulties as direct evidence of ability, reducing comparison with others.

positive_force: The real achievement of completing the Appalachian Trail; evidence of persistence and endurance
Has some self-observation ability, able to identify negative thought patterns and trigger situations
Willing to seek help and accept counseling; motivation is clear
At specific highly difficult moments, can experience pride and a sense of value
negative_force: Excessively high and rigid self-standards (perfectionistic tendency)
Persistent comparison and Self-deprecation (negating the positive, mental filtering)
Mind-reading and future-predicting negative Anticipation (worrying about being seen through as an 'impostor')
Social avoidance, weakening the integration of support systems and positive feedback

antecedent: When thinking about or being reminded of outdoor activities
Anticipating being judged or 'exposed as inadequate'
target_behavior.core_reason: Having internalized the belief that 'one must meet high standards to be qualified', worrying about being exposed as incompetent, generating catastrophic Anticipation and shame.
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome consequences (being judged/shame), reducing Anxiety in the short term; maintaining consistency with the 'I am not good enough' self-schema.
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced interest and pleasure, missed opportunities for positive experiences and revising beliefs about ability, weakened social connection.

target_behavior.behavior: Verbally negating when receiving positive feedback (e.g. 'they are just being polite')
antecedent: Others' praise for one's hiking or writing
Being affirmed in conversations reviewing achievements
target_behavior.core_reason: To maintain the 'I am not good enough' core belief and avoid vulnerability, Rationalizing or Projecting external positive information as unreal.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding inner conflict and cognitive dissonance, protecting self-esteem from being shaken; reducing Anxiety in the short term.
target_behavior.consequence: Positive feedback hard to internalize, Reinforcement of Negative self-evaluation, further lowering motivation and Self-efficacy.
